definitions.explanation: A flat mat woven from rushes (igusa) or similar plant materials. Used for sitting or lying on outdoors, at festivals, picnics, and traditional events. Also refers to the woven surface layer of tatami.

examples.japanese: {花見|はなみ}のためにござを{敷|し}いた。
examples.english: I spread out a mat for cherry blossom viewing.

examples.japanese: ござの{上|うえ}に{座|すわ}って{弁当|べんとう}を{食|た}べた。
examples.english: I sat on the rush mat and ate my boxed lunch.

examples.japanese: {夏祭|なつまつ}りの{会場|かいじょう}にはござが{何枚|なんまい}も{並|なら}べられていた。
examples.english: Many rush mats were laid out at the summer festival venue.

notes:
USAGE:
Commonly associated with outdoor events like {花見|はなみ} (cherry blossom viewing), {花火大会|はなびたいかい} (fireworks festivals), and picnics. The word can also refer to the woven rush surface of {畳|たたみ}, known as ござ{目|め}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ござを{敷|し}く (to spread out a mat)
- ござの{上|うえ} (on the mat)
- {花見|はなみ}ござ (cherry blossom viewing mat)

WRITING:
Sometimes written as {茣蓙|ござ}, but the kana form is far more common in modern usage.
